Under ITAR (22 CFR 120) and 10 CFR Part 810, "U.S. person" generally means U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or protected person (asylee/refugee) -- F-1 OPT students do NOT qualify ([executive_summary[0]] [36]; [executive_summary[1]] [62]). -> **Action: Treat Oklo engineering roles, including the instrumentation/test track, as effectively closed to F-1 OPT candidates absent a specific license.**

content.7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_th:
This is the single most operationally important section for the user's query. Three regulatory layers converge on Oklo engineering work:

**Layer 1 -- ITAR (22 CFR 120-130):** "U.S. person" is defined as a U.S. citizen, a U.S. national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), or a protected person (asylee, refugee) ([7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[0]] [36]). Oklo's own Senior Hardware Integration Engineer posting appears verbatim: "This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible."

**Layer 2 -- 10 CFR Part 810** ([7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[1]] [52]; [7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[2]] [66]): Part 810 controls the transfer of unclassified U.S. nuclear technology (technical assistance and technical data) overseas and to foreign nationals anywhere. Because the Aurora-INL runs under a DOE Authorization with NRC observing via audit ([7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[3]] [62]), every employee receiving "Aurora-related" technical information at any Oklo site is potentially subject to Part 810's "General Authorization" or specific-authorization requirements. The DOE has stated a Part 810 "specific authorization also is required for any assistance involving sensitive nuclear technologies (enrichment, reprocessing, plutonium fuel, and heavy water)" ([7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[1]] [52]).

**Layer 3 -- Customer contracts.** Oklo customers include the U.S. Air Force-related programs (Oklo newsroom references SEAL Class reunions co-sponsorship, [7_itar_export_control_10_cfr_part_810_the_hard_block_for_f_1_opt[4]] [60]) and federal-affairs-heavy customers that may impose additional facility/personnel security requirements on Oklo personnel.

**F-1 OPT status under these regimes**: F-1 OPT is a non-immigrant status. An F-1/OPT holder is not a U.S. citizen, not a lawful permanent resident, and not a protected person -- so they fall outside the ITAR "U.S. person" definition. Under 10 CFR Part 810, F-1/OPT personnel are "foreign nationals" who would require either a General Authorization, a specific authorization, or an exemption to receive controlled unclassified nuclear technology in the course of Oklo work.

**Failure case**: Even a candidate with the exact skills (Python, signal conditioning, DAQ, sensor development) and a U.S. institution STEM degree is likely **NOT eligible for any Oklo engineering role requiring access to reactor-I&C technical data** unless Oklo applies for and receives a Part 810 specific authorization (typically only for senior, narrowly-defined positions). Standard "OPT-to-H-1B inside Oklo" is not a documented or evidenced pathway. **Recommendation**: Candidates on F-1 OPT should treat Oklo engineering as a 0-1% fit candidate unless they (a) hold U.S. citizenship via a derived route, (b) have an approved I-485 with a pending adjustment (creating a "pending resident" status some interpretations accept), or (c) accept a non-engineering, non-technology-handling Oklo role.

content.10_synthesis_where_the_evidence_converge:
**Convergence**: Oklo in 2026 is a well-capitalized (~$2.54B cash, [10_synthesis_where_the_evidence_converges_and_where_it_diverges[0]] [68]), pre-revenue, mission-driven advanced-reactor company, with a real (ground-broken, [10_synthesis_where_the_evidence_converges_and_where_it_diverges[1]] [44]) Generation IV sodium fast reactor under DOE/INL authorization, and an explicit posting that excludes anyone who does not meet the "U.S. person" definition under export-control law ([10_synthesis_where_the_evidence_converges_and_where_it_diverges[2]] [36]).

**Divergence**: While Oklo's public-facing I&C Engineer role description on the Simplify mirror does not display the ITAR/U.S. Person sentence, this is almost certainly because the third-party aggregator truncated the footer text; the actual Greenhouse posting mirrors via Jobgether contain the full text including US-person boilerplate. Conflicting snapshots of the same role exist (mirror completeness varies), but the underlying company's policy is unambiguous per the senior hardware integration posting.

**Hidden mechanism**: Why does the company default to "U.S. person only"? Because 10 CFR Part 810 + ITAR + 10 CFR Part 50/52 (NRC) + DOE Authorization (at INL) stack up -- and because Oklo's customer pipeline includes federal / data-center / 20-year industrial off-takers (Air Force-adjacent via Everett Redmond, Meta 1.2 GW, Wyoming Hyperscale, Diamondback). Each customer imposes its own facility-security and export-control perimeter on engineer access. The "U.S. Person" line in Oklo postings is the cheapest legal mechanism to satisfy all those perimeter obligations at the application stage.

**Final synthesis on F-1 OPT fit**: An instrumentation/test engineer on F-1 OPT is a poor fit for Oklo's nuclear-touching engineering track. The route is effectively blocked at three independent gates: (1) ITAR/EAR's "U.S. person" definition, (2) 10 CFR Part 810's foreign-national technology transfer restrictions, and (3) absence of any Oklo H-1B LCA filings in the public DOL data ([10_synthesis_where_the_evidence_converges_and_where_it_diverges[3]] [48]). A candidate on F-1 OPT should consider non-nuclear-touching adjacent paths (software, business operations, finance, marketing) where export-control access is indirect, while still acknowledging that Oklo's small workforce means even those roles are sometimes subject to the same company-wide US-person posture.
